question.text: How many cumulative confirmed Ebola cases will the DRC's 2026 outbreak have reported as of October 31, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the cumulative number of laboratory-confirmed cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo's 2026 Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) outbreak, as reported for the reporting date of 31 October 2026 (or, if that exact date is not available, the latest reporting date on or before 31 October 2026) in official situation reporting. The primary source is the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) outbreak page (https://www.ecdc.europa.eu/en/ebola-outbreak-democratic-republic-congo-and-uganda), which is updated every weekday and reports the DRC cumulative confirmed case total; the DRC INSP daily situation reports (https://insp.cd/category/sitrep/) or other [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) may be used if the ECDC figure is unavailable. For example, a report of 10,250 confirmed cases resolves as 10250. Only confirmed cases (not suspected or probable) in the DRC count.
question.fine_print: The figure used is the cumulative DRC confirmed-case total attributed to the reporting date of 31 October 2026; because sources report on a lag, the value reflected for that reporting date in a report published in early November 2026 will be used. If no source reports a figure for any reporting date between 26 and 31 October 2026, resolution waits until such data is published. If the ECDC and INSP sources and all other credible sources permanently discontinue reporting this total before any figure for a reporting date on or after 26 October 2026 appears, the question is annulled. Figures for Uganda or any country other than the DRC are excluded.

research:
I've finished the searches and am writing up. Note that the newest official figure I could get is for 23 October, eight reporting days before the resolution date.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-10-21: The ECDC page shows **9,704 confirmed DRC cases and 4,687 deaths**, using data up to 20 October. It had not been updated past that when I fetched it on 26 October. It gives no daily series. [ECDC](https://www.ecdc.europa.eu/en/ebola-outbreak-democratic-republic-congo-and-uganda)
- 2026-10-25: The newest INSP sitrep listed is **N°162, for 23/10/2026**, posted 25 October. Sitreps appear 1 to 2 days after their reporting date (N°160 and N°161 were both posted 24 October). The listing page shows no figures and I could not open the PDFs. [INSP](https://insp.cd/category/sitrep/)
- 2026-10-23: An outbreak tracker citing INSP SitRep 162 gives **9,876 confirmed cases and 4,803 deaths** as of 23 October. [ebola-tracker.org](https://ebola-tracker.org/en/)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The latest confirmed figure is 9,876 for 23 October, and eight reporting days remain until 31 October.
- 2026-10-23: 60 new confirmed cases were reported in four provinces: North Kivu 29, Ituri 28, Haut-Uele 2, Tshopo 1. Ituri has 72.2% of all cases. North Kivu's share of new cases is growing. This comes from a Substack newsletter, as summarized in search results (the page itself returned an error). [Outbreak News Today](https://outbreaknewstoday.substack.com/p/ebola-outbreak-update-as-of-october-3eb)
- 2026-10-22: The DRC communications ministry gave **9,816 confirmed, 4,757 deaths**, 2,635 recovered and 1,130 in isolation. That matches 9,876 minus 60. [AA](https://www.aa.com.tr/fr/sante/rdc-l-%C3%A9pid%C3%A9mie-d-ebola-atteint-9-816-cas-confirm%C3%A9s-dont-4-757-d%C3%A9c%C3%A8s-selon-les-autorit%C3%A9s/4099679)
- Wikipedia's provincial table labels 9,876 as "22 October", one day off from the other sources. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Central_Africa_Ebola_epidemic)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-26: Investigators are looking at whether Ebola cases in Kenya and Nigeria are linked through Entebbe airport (a possible overlap on 3 October). No transmission there has been shown. [TTW](https://www.travelandtourworld.com/news/article/k2e2upm05x85/)
- 2026-10-24: The US CDC lists 8 affected DRC provinces: Bas-Uele, Haut-Uele, Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Sud-Ubangi, Nord-Ubangi and Tshopo. [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/ebola/situation-summary/index.html)
- 2026-10-23: Kenya reported its second death and 9 confirmed cases in total. Uganda tightened border controls. [Xinhua](https://www.news.cn/20261024/034106219c884090bcef9093c1ab4f8e/c.html)
- 2026-10-23: The Tumaini Phase 2/3 Bundibugyo vaccine trial started in Bunia. [SocialNews](https://www.socialnews.xyz/2026/10/23/major-ebola-vaccine-trial-begins-in-dr-congo-as-outbreak-continues/)
- 2026-10-20: The DRC had 9,704 cases with 67 new in 24 hours, according to a French article. Nigeria confirmed its first case. [LMOUS](https://www.lesmotsontunsens.com/rdc-ouganda-kenya-nigeria-ebola-continue-de-setendre/)
- 2026-10-15: WHO, via UN News, described transmission as "high and fluctuating" across 65 health zones. [UN News](https://news.un.org/fr/story/2026/10/1159669)

## 4. Base rates and trend
DRC cumulative confirmed cases, with the daily rates calculated by me:

| Date | Cumulative | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 27 Sep | 8,000 | Wikipedia |
| 6 Oct | 8,728 | WHO DON619 (question background) |
| 10 Oct | 9,000 | Wikipedia |
| 12 Oct | 9,144 | question background |
| 14 Oct | ~9,277 | question background |
| 20 Oct | 9,704 | ECDC / LMOUS |
| 22 Oct | 9,816 | AA |
| 23 Oct | 9,876 | INSP via tracker |

- Weekly new confirmed cases from the tracker: 5 to 11 October, 462 (about 66 a day); 12 to 18 October, 487 (about 70 a day). [ebola-tracker.org](https://ebola-tracker.org/en/)
- Average daily rates: 6 to 23 October, about 67.5; 14 to 23 October, about 66.6; 20 to 23 October, about 57 (112 over two days, then 60).
- Single days run from about 56 to 79. Over the past month the rate has been flat to slightly falling, not speeding up.
- Simple projection (my arithmetic, not a forecast): 8 more days at 50, 57, 67 or 75 a day would give about 10,276, 10,332, 10,412 or 10,476. Even 40 a day gives about 10,196, and 90 a day gives about 10,596. Totals at the edges of the question's range (9,277 to 11,500) would need near-zero or more than 200 cases a day.
- Caveats: different outlets date the same figure differently, by up to a day. ECDC sometimes lags several days behind INSP. Backlogs of lab results could make single days jump.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market or Metaculus question on DRC cumulative confirmed cases.
- Related markets:
  - Kalshi "Ebola pandemic in 2026": 4%.
  - Polymarket "Ebola pandemic in 2026": 2.5%.
  - Kalshi, countries reporting a case before 2027: CAR 57%, South Sudan 40%, Tanzania 36%.
  - Polymarket "countries with an Ebola case in 2026": South Sudan 35%, Rwanda 22%.
- These suggest traders see the spread as continuing but contained. None bears directly on the DRC count.
- I found no published expert projection of the DRC case count for late October.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- INSP sitreps for 24 to 31 October should be posted from about 26 October to 2 November. ECDC updates on weekdays and has been lagging INSP by a few days. The question uses the figure for the 31 October reporting date as published in early November.
- Things that could push the count up: the shift toward North Kivu, newly affected Nord-Ubangi, and international spread to Kenya and Nigeria. Testing backlogs being cleared could also cause one-day jumps.
- Things that could slow it: the maturing response (MSF treatment centers) and the new Tumaini vaccine trial, though the trial is unlikely to change incidence within 8 days.
- Possible reporting problems: sources dating figures differently, and ECDC's lag. If ECDC's page is stale, the resolver may fall back on INSP.

forecasts.reasoning:
**(a) Time left:** The outcome depends on reporting through 31 October, which is 8 reporting days after the latest figure. Final data should be published by about 2 to 7 November.

**(b) Latest known value:** 9,876 confirmed cases for 23 October (INSP SitRep 162, via the tracker). This is consistent with 9,816 for 22 October from the DRC communications ministry. The latest figure on the ECDC page is 9,704, using data to 20 October.

**(c) If nothing changed:** About 9,876.

**(d) If the current trend continued:** The rate has been 57 to 67 confirmed cases a day, flat to slightly falling. Eight more days at about 60 a day gives about 10,360. At 67 a day it gives about 10,410.

**(e) Historical variation:** Daily counts have ranged from about 55 to 80. Weekly totals were 460 to 490. Over 8 days that means roughly 400 to 600 added, plus possible backlog jumps. Outlets also sometimes date the same figure one day apart, which adds about 60 cases of uncertainty.

**(f) Experts and markets:** No market or expert projection exists for this count. WHO describes transmission as "high and fluctuating." Related markets suggest the outbreak is spreading but contained, with no sign of explosive growth.

**(g) Unexpected scenarios:**
- Low: insecurity or lab or reporting disruptions in Ituri and North Kivu, or a sharp drop in testing, push daily confirmed cases down to 20 to 40. That would give about 10,100 to 10,200.
- High: North Kivu or newly affected provinces accelerate, or a cleared testing backlog adds a one-day jump of several hundred. That would give 10,600 or more.
